divergence:
Three deltas, all on one event; none is a key-name mismatch — there is no value being carried under a wrong key.

1. WRONG OCCURRENCE. Documented trigger is "a user-typed command expands into a prompt"; ours is "a turn is about to be sent" (`pi-agent.ts:6565` → `:6418`). It over-fires on every plain prompt with no command, and it is keyed to the turn, not to the expansion.
2. EMPTY PAYLOAD. All five documented fields (`expansion_type`, `command_name`, `command_args`, `command_source`, `prompt`) are absent from the emission AND from the `SdkAutomationInput` type. Command hooks read stdin as a spread of that input (`packages/shared/src/automations/hook-command.ts:641-651`), so a hook script reading `command_name` gets `undefined`.
3. INERT MATCHER. `Matches on `command_name`` is unimplemented (`utils.ts:221-238`), so the documented recipe (a hook matching `deploy` gating `/deploy`) can never run; the registrar warns about it (`hooks-automation.ts:349`) rather than supporting it.

Block semantics are the one half that is already right: `UserPromptExpansion` is in `TERMINAL_BLOCK_AGENT_EVENTS`-style handling (`packages/shared/src/automations/hook-decision-contract.ts:42`, `:240`) and the gate turns a block into an ended turn (`pi-agent.ts:6430-6432`, `:6566-6569`). But because the gate runs AFTER the RPC handler already expanded the command, a block does not "prevent the command from expanding": `resolveCustomSlashCommand` (sessions.ts:323 — which for an MCP command has already called `getPrompt` on the server) and `updateSessionModel` (sessions.ts:342) have both already run.

userImpact:
Two concrete failures, both on imported plugins that ship hooks (the only surface that can register this event today).

1. The doc's own use case is dead. A user installs a Claude plugin whose `hooks.json` has a `UserPromptExpansion` entry with `"matcher": "deploy"` (block `/deploy` unless an approval file exists). Sources → plugin install shows a warning — "declares a matcher on UserPromptExpansion, which has no matcher value in Nessy, so the hook never runs" (`hooks-automation.ts:767`) — and typing `/deploy` in the composer runs the command with no gate. The guard the user installed silently does nothing.

2. A matcher-less hook fires on the wrong events with an empty payload. It runs once per turn on EVERY prompt, including plain typed messages with no slash command (`pi-agent.ts:6565` → `:6418`), and its stdin JSON contains `{hook_event_name, source: 'pi-before-agent-start', lifecycle_version: 1}` and nothing else. A logging hook records one row per turn instead of one per command and cannot say which command; a gating hook that reads `command_name` sees `undefined` and either no-ops or, if it blocks by default, kills every turn in the session with "A UserPromptExpansion hook blocked this prompt."

Latent third: even with a hook that does block, `/mycommand` has already been expanded server-side by then — for an MCP prompt command the remote `getPrompt` call already happened, and a command carrying `model:` has already switched the session model (sessions.ts:342). The user sees the turn refused but the model in the composer changed anyway.
notes: Every path cited was read this session (codegraph verbatim source plus direct reads); the absence claims used `grep -ran` over `packages apps scripts`, with `-a` for the NUL-byte files. Two things rest on reading rather than a live run: (a) the ordering claim that a block arrives after `getPrompt`/`updateSessionModel` have run is derived from `sessions.ts:317-343` executing before `sessionManager.sendMessage` at :362-375, not from an observed session; (b) I did not check whether `apps/cli` has its own expansion path — if it does, it needs the same emission. Also unspecified upstream: hooks.md gives no vocabulary for `command_source` beyond the single example value `"plugin"`, so our `CustomSlashCommandSource` union (`nessy-agent | agents | plugin | skill | mcp | workflow`, `packages/shared/src/slash-commands/common.ts:4`) lines up for `plugin`/`skill`/`mcp` and has no documented counterpart for the two native sources — pick a stable spelling and record it, rather than guessing at Claude's.
